title: Cross product and oriented area

source_policy: Primary references support definitions and stated conditions. Workshop stories and worked derivations are originally authored constructions. The supplied book matrix guides sequencing; it is not independent verification of a book edition or lesson.
purpose: Rotate one measured edge, follow the perpendicular component into parallelogram area, and keep the normal direction separate from magnitude.
meaning: In an oriented Euclidean three-dimensional space, the cross product of two vectors is perpendicular to both. Its magnitude is their parallelogram area; its direction follows the chosen right-handed orientation. Reversing the order reverses the product. The executable family keeps both input vectors in the coordinate plane, so the product has only a signed z component.

definition.setting: A planar family of vectors inside a fixed right-handed orthonormal three-dimensional coordinate frame.
definition.formal_latex: \mathbf u=(a,0,0),\quad\mathbf v=(b\cos\theta,b\sin\theta,0),\quad\mathbf u\times\mathbf v=(0,0,ab\sin\theta),\quad A=\lVert\mathbf u\times\mathbf v\rVert.

signature.θ: Signed angle from u toward v.

conditions: The reference frame is orthonormal and right-handed, with positive z directed out of the input plane.
The lengths a and b lie from zero to four metres. The signed planar angle θ lies from −180 to 180 degrees; negative angles turn below the positive x axis.
The input vectors are u=(a,0,0) and v=(b cosθ,b sinθ,0). Their cross product points only in the z direction and its signed component is a b sinθ square metres.

Unoriented area A is the nonnegative magnitude |a b sinθ|. A zero product has no distinguished normal direction, including parallel inputs and a zero vector. When either length is zero, θ remains the construction's orientation parameter; it is not an angle defined by two nonzero vectors.
definition.domain_notes: The broader cross-product definition applies to three-dimensional vectors in an oriented Euclidean frame. This executable planar family illustrates its component formula, magnitude and orientation without being an arbitrary 3D vector editor.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources and original restricted-family arguments; independent review pending.

grammar.expression_latex: \mathbf u=(a,0,0),\quad\mathbf v=(b\cos\theta,b\sin\theta,0),\quad\mathbf u\times\mathbf v=(0,0,ab\sin\theta),\quad A=\lVert\mathbf u\times\mathbf v\rVert.
grammar.formation_rule: Set u=(a,0,0) and v=(b cosθ,b sinθ,0). The general component rule gives u×v=(u_yv_z−u_zv_y,u_zv_x−u_xv_z,u_xv_y−u_yv_x). In this family w_z=a b sinθ and A=|w_z|. The displayed angle is in degrees.
grammar.precedence: Compute the components of v from the signed angle, then form the ordered cross product u×v. Take absolute value only when reading the unoriented area.

prompts.prompt: Why does the area stay nonnegative when the normal reverses?
prompts.answer: Orientation belongs to the signed vector product. Unoriented area is its magnitude, so it is nonnegative.

prompts.prompt: What happens when the edges become parallel?
prompts.answer: Their perpendicular separation is zero, so the parallelogram area and cross product are zero.
